text:
Alice: Hey team, customer hitting intermittent embed dim flips on /v1/embeddings. Sometimes vectors come back length 1023 instead of 1024. Happening only when requests go through their HTTP/2 reverse proxy. Request IDs: r-0a7f3e, r-0a7f3f, r-0a7f40.

Ben: Can you drop a minimal curl repro and one example response?

Alice: Repro curl we gave them (they say this triggers ~1/20):
```bash
curl -v --http2 \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a7f3e" \n  --data-binary @payload.gz \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings?rwd_model=rwd-embed-v2
```
payload.json (before gzip):
```json
{"input":["doc1","doc2","doc3","doc4"],"batch":true}
```

Alice: Example server-side response body they observed (trimmed):
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, ...],"object":"embedding"}, {"embedding":[... 1023 floats ...],"object":"embedding"}],"model":"rwd-embed-v2"}
```

Carla: I pulled the ingress logs for r-0a7f3e. Envoy shows: `:method: POST`, `transfer-encoding: chunked`, no content-length. Then upstream request to runtime shows `content-length: 13568`. Looks like proxy is buffering/chunking and our ingress is adding a content-length when forwarding.

Carla: Log snippet (ingress):
```
[2026-03-01T12:02:11Z] r-0a7f3e route_inbound: headers={":method":"POST", ":path":"/v1/embeddings" , "transfer-encoding":"chunked", "content-encoding":"gzip"}
[2026-03-01T12:02:11Z] r-0a7f3e body_received: chunks=6 total_bytes=13568
```
Dave: This smells like a chunk boundary aligning with a compression block such that when we ungzip+re-chunk we accidentally drop a byte at the end of a float array serialization in one codepath. Rare but plausible.

Ben: Can we reproduce internally by forcing chunked transfer-encoding with gzip? I'll try a quick python http/2 client. Meanwhile, can you collect: full raw tcpdump (client->ingress), ingress logs (with raw headers), runtime request log, and the exact gz payload (payload.gz) for those request IDs?

Alice: Collected artifacts attached in the ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/INC-3245 (includes payload.gz, raw tcpdump pcap, ingress logs).

infra-bot: Automated checklist: please run `./scripts/collect-debug-bundle --ids r-0a7f3e,r-0a7f3f,r-0a7f40 --include-pcap --include-runtime-logs` and upload to S3. Also attach the client's proxy config if available.

Carla: I also see a runtime warning right before the dim-flip: `kv_cache_deserialize: expected 8192 bytes, got 8191`. That off-by-one could shift float boundaries in the JSON encoder in rare cases.

Dave: Proposed repro steps for eng-runtime:
1) Use the exact payload.gz from ticket.
2) Run a small proxy that forwards with chunked semantics (nghttpx or curl --http2 --raw) to simulate their proxy.
3) Run throughput/fuzz where chunk sizes vary (random 64-512 bytes) to try to force the alignment.

Ben: I'll try with nghttpx + our local runtime image, will report back with deterministic tracer. If I can reproduce, next step is a tight unit test around the gzip+chunk reassembly path.

Alice: For support ops: ask the customer to temporarily bypass their proxy or force content-length header to see if it stops. If that helps, we narrow to proxy behavior.

support-bot: Created escalation ticket ESCL-842. Assigned eng-runtime (@dave) and infra (@carla). Priority: P2.

Carla: One more note — the bad responses always include `content-encoding: identity` between ingress and runtime in a handful of traces, meaning some intermediate removed gzip header but passed compressed body bytes. That would definitely cause a garbage float count after decode. Please include checks for consistent content-encoding handling in the proxy chain.

Dave: OK, I'll focus on reassembly edge cases and gzip header passthrough. Ben — ping me once you have repro.

Ben: Will do. Tracking here. :mag:
